Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were married on 13.10.2018 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
Out of the said wedlock, no child was born.

sentences.text:
Further, after marriage, the petitioner no. 1 and his family members had insulted the respondent no.
2 as wedding arrangements were not up to their expectations.

It is stated that the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 went to their honeymoon wherein, petitioner no. 1 had consumed heavy alcohol, when the same was objected by respondent no. 2, the petitioner no. 1 herein under the influence of alcohol had threatened and had fought with the respondent no. 2.
A similar incident had occurred where both the parties went to Agra thereafter.

Soon after, petitioner no. 1 had apologized for his behaviour but on 30.10.2018, petitioner no. 1 under the influence of alcohol had abused and fought with the respondent no. 2 threatening her not to indulge in his life.
Petitioner no.1s habit of habitually consuming of alcohol was concealed from respondent no. 2 before marriage.
Thereafter, respondent no. 2 was suggested to be operated and still petitioner no. 1 had visited to the hospital intoxicated.
Even petitioner no. 1 threatened respondent no. 2 stating not to disclose these acts to anyone else.
Petitioners had often abused respondent no. 2 not only physically but also mentally as well as sexually for unfilled dowry and often demands.
7. On the complaint of respondent no. 2, the present FIR was registered against the petitioners.

It is stated that during the pendency of the case, both the parties have amicably settled all their disputes before before learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, Saket, (South), New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 17.10.2023.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, Saket, (South), New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is stated that marriage has been dissolved by way of mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 18.12.2023.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, Saket, (South),
New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 17.10.2023 and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
9.

entities.text:
Principal Judge, Family Courts, Saket, (South),
New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter,
this Court is of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 0192/2023 registered at Police Station Ambedkar Nagar, New Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed, subject to petitioners depositing a cost of Rs.
15,000/- with Delhi High Court Bar Association Advocates Welfare Fund within 15 days.
